sop_modules.name: Exterior Stucco Protection & Equipment Setup
sop_modules.description: Deploy landscape/hardscape protection, mask light fixtures and HVAC units, set up spray equipment (conditional on spray_backroll). Window/door glass protection is NOT this spec's responsibility — belongs in window/door specs.

tasks.name: Landscape Perimeter Protection
tasks.description: Deploy tarps and plastic sheeting along house perimeter where landscape is adjacent to stucco wall. Measured in linear feet along the foundation/stucco wall line. Full cover for spray_backroll (10-15 ft overspray drift), edge tarps for roll-only.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of plantings within spray drift zone. Secure tarps against wind with stakes or weights. UV-resistant 4 mil plastic minimum for multi-day stucco projects.

tasks.name: Walkway Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over walkways adjacent to stucco wall. Canvas for crew traffic areas (non-slip). Tape plastic to foundation at grade line using red stucco tape for textured stucco surfaces.

quality_notes.all: Tape plastic to foundation at grade line using red stucco tape. Extend coverage to overspray zone. Canvas for crew traffic areas.

tasks.name: Patio Protection Setup
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over patio areas adjacent to stucco wall. Conditional — only when patio present.

quality_notes.all: Full coverage of patio surface within overspray drift zone. Secure plastic with weights. Canvas for crew traffic paths.

tasks.name: Light Fixture Masking
tasks.description: Mask exterior light fixtures with tape and plastic bags. Use blue masking tape on smooth fixture surfaces — stucco tape not needed on non-stucco surfaces.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of all fixtures on working elevation. Secure plastic to prevent wind displacement.

tasks.name: HVAC Unit Cover
tasks.description: Bag and tarp HVAC condenser units adjacent to stucco wall. Conditional — only when HVAC unit present. Do not block intake/exhaust if unit is running.

quality_notes.all: Full cover of condenser unit. Secure with weights — wind can dislodge loose covering. Do not block HVAC intake/exhaust if unit is running.

tasks.name: Spray Equipment Setup
tasks.description: Set up ladders, scaffold, or lift per access_type. Configure airless sprayer: 517 tip + 60-mesh filter for primer/acrylic finish, OR 521-525 tip + 30-mesh filter for elastomeric. Stage 18-inch roller frame + thick-nap covers for mandatory backroll. Two-person crew minimum for spray_backroll.

quality_notes.all: Verify tip size matches material: 517 for acrylic/primer, 521-525 for elastomeric. Verify filter mesh: 60-mesh (black) for latex, 30-mesh (gray) for elastomeric. Stage roller alongside sprayer — backroll is MANDATORY on all stucco spray operations. Two-person crew minimum.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Landscape protection -> Hardscape protection (walk, patio) -> Fixture masking -> HVAC cover -> Spray equipment setup (if spray_backroll).

sop_modules.name: Exterior Stucco Surface Preparation
sop_modules.description: Stucco prep sequence: crack assessment FIRST (>1/8 inch = HARD STOP), EIFS knock test (EIFS only — delamination = HARD STOP), moisture test (traditional stucco, MC <12% hard stop), cure verification (traditional stucco, 30-day standard / 7-day with alkali-resistant primer), pressure wash (branched by substrate_type: 1,500-3,000 PSI traditional vs <500 PSI EIFS), mildew treatment (conditional), efflorescence treatment (traditional only, conditional), crack patching (<1/8 inch cosmetic), surface defect patching, caulk stucco-to-trim joints, EIFS insurance verification (EIFS only).

tasks.name: Crack Assessment
tasks.description: FIRST task in prep — assess all stucco surfaces for cracking BEFORE any other work. Document crack width, pattern, and location per elevation. Cracks >1/8 inch = HARD STOP — indicates structural movement, requires engineering evaluation before coating. Cosmetic cracks <1/8 inch can be patched. Crack mapping is mandatory documentation for both traditional stucco and EIFS.

quality_notes.all: FIRST task — no other prep work begins until crack assessment is complete. Measure crack widths with crack gauge. Document crack patterns: random hairline (cosmetic) vs. patterned/diagonal (structural). Cracks >1/8 inch = HARD STOP, refer to structural engineer. Cracks at window/door corners may indicate header movement.

tasks.name: EIFS Knock Test
tasks.description: Systematic knock test on EIFS surfaces per elevation. Identify delamination between EPS foam and substrate or between base coat and finish coat. Hollow/drum sound = delamination = HARD STOP — EIFS must be repaired by EIFS specialist before any coating work. EIFS substrate only.

quality_notes.all: Systematic grid pattern — tap every 2-3 ft. Solid/dense sound = good bond. Hollow/drum sound = delamination. Mark all delaminated areas. ANY delamination = HARD STOP. EIFS repair is NOT a painting task — refer to EIFS specialist.

tasks.name: Moisture Content Testing
tasks.description: Test moisture content of traditional stucco surface. Must read <12% MC before any coating application. Test methods: electronic moisture meter, ASTM D4263 (Plastic Sheet Method). MC >12% is a HARD STOP — do not coat. Traditional stucco only — EIFS has different moisture management via drainage plane.

quality_notes.QT2: Spot check representative areas on each elevation.
quality_notes.QT3: Check multiple points per elevation. Document readings.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic check grid pattern. All readings documented. Every area must pass <12% MC.

tasks.name: Cure Time Verification
tasks.description: Verify traditional stucco cure status. Standard: 30 days from application. Accelerated: 7 days minimum when alkali-resistant primer is specified. Document cure date from construction schedule. If cure time insufficient, HARD STOP — do not proceed. Traditional stucco only — EIFS acrylic finish is factory-cured.

quality_notes.all: Verify cure date from GC or construction schedule. Document in project file. 7-day accelerated path REQUIRES alkali-resistant primer — no exceptions. Standard 30-day cure applies when non-alkali-resistant primer is used.

tasks.name: Pressure Wash — Traditional Stucco
tasks.description: Power wash traditional stucco wall to remove construction dust, dirt, debris, and loose material. Use 1,500-3,000 PSI — sufficient for stucco cleaning without surface damage. Allow 24-48 hr dry time before coating. Re-verify MC <12% after drying.

quality_notes.QT2: Basic power wash to remove visible dirt and debris.
quality_notes.QT3: Full power wash with detergent. Rinse thoroughly. Allow 24-48 hr dry time.
quality_notes.QT4: Full power wash with TSP solution. Rinse thoroughly. Allow 48 hr dry time minimum. Moisture meter check mandatory before proceeding.

tasks.name: Low-Pressure Wash — EIFS
tasks.description: Gentle wash EIFS surfaces with <500 PSI and wide fan tip. EIFS is vulnerable to impact damage from high-pressure water. Do NOT exceed 500 PSI. Wide fan pattern to distribute pressure. Remove construction dust, dirt, and biological growth without damaging acrylic finish coat or EPS substrate.

quality_notes.QT2: Basic gentle wash to remove visible dirt.
quality_notes.QT3: Full gentle wash. Detergent if needed. Keep pressure under 500 PSI at all times.
quality_notes.QT4: Thorough gentle wash with mild detergent. Rinse completely. Inspect for damage to existing EIFS finish coat.

tasks.name: Mildew Treatment
tasks.description: Eradicate mildew/biological growth on stucco surfaces. Solution: 1:3 bleach to water. Apply, dwell 15-20 minutes, scrub with stiff bristle brush, rinse thoroughly. Must complete before any coating. Conditional — only when mildew is present. Applies to both traditional stucco and EIFS.

quality_notes.QT2: Treat visible mildew areas. Bleach solution, scrub, rinse.
quality_notes.QT3: Full treatment of all mildew areas. Verify eradication before coating.
quality_notes.QT4: Full treatment. Repeat application if needed. Document treatment. Verify no recurrence during cure period.

tasks.name: Efflorescence Treatment
tasks.description: Remove efflorescence (white salt deposits) from traditional stucco surfaces. Cleaning hierarchy: (1) water + stiff brush (light), (2) TSP solution (moderate), (3) phosphoric acid (severe). Conditional — only when efflorescence is present. Traditional stucco only — EIFS does not effloresce (not cementitious).

quality_notes.QT2: Brush off loose efflorescence. Water wash.
quality_notes.QT3: Full removal with TSP if moderate. Verify moisture source addressed.
quality_notes.QT4: Complete removal. TSP or acid wash as required. Document treatment and verify no recurrence before coating.

tasks.name: Cosmetic Crack Patching
tasks.description: Patch cosmetic cracks <1/8 inch with elastomeric crack sealant. Only cracks identified during crack assessment that are below the 1/8 inch structural threshold. Allow sealant to cure (24-48 hours latex-based, 3-7 days polyurethane) before coating. Conditional — only when cosmetic cracks are present.

quality_notes.QT3: Fill all identified cracks <1/8 inch. Tool smooth. Allow full cure before coating.
quality_notes.QT4: Fill all cracks. Precision tooling for invisible repair. Texture match at patch location. Full cure verified before coating.

tasks.name: Surface Defect Patching
tasks.description: Patch minor surface defects — spalled areas, impact damage, and localized deterioration. Patch material must match existing stucco texture profile. Texture match is critical — visible patches are a quality failure. Conditional — only when surface defects are present.

quality_notes.QT3: Repair obvious defects. Texture match to surrounding area.
quality_notes.QT4: Repair all defects. Perfect texture match. Patch must be invisible after coating.

tasks.name: Caulk Stucco-to-Trim Joints
tasks.description: Apply polyurethane exterior caulk (Class 25/50) to stucco-to-trim joints: stucco-to-window casings, stucco-to-door casings, stucco-to-soffit transitions, stucco-to-frieze board. Use red stucco tape for masking on stucco side. 3-7 day cure before painting. Do NOT use silicone — not paintable.

quality_notes.QT3: All stucco-to-trim joints caulked. Smooth tool. Clean edges.
quality_notes.QT4: All joints caulked with consistent bead. Precision tool smooth. Mask both sides with stucco tape on stucco and blue tape on trim.

tasks.name: EIFS Insurance Verification
tasks.description: Verify CGL insurance covers EIFS work or obtain EIFS-specific rider before starting any coating work on EIFS substrate. Administrative gate — CGL policies commonly exclude EIFS work. Document verification in project file. EIFS only.

quality_notes.all: Administrative task. Verify insurance documentation before starting EIFS work. Document verification in project file. No exceptions.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Crack assessment FIRST (hard stop at >1/8 inch) -> EIFS knock test (EIFS only, hard stop on delamination) -> Moisture test (traditional, hard stop at >12% MC) -> Cure verification (traditional) -> EIFS insurance verification (EIFS only) -> Pressure wash (branched by substrate_type) -> Dry time (24-48 hr) -> Mildew treatment (conditional) -> Efflorescence treatment (traditional, conditional) -> Crack patching (conditional) -> Surface patching -> Caulk joints.

sop_modules.name: Stucco Primer Application
sop_modules.description: Full field prime coat. Primer selection branched by substrate_type: alkali-resistant primer on traditional stucco (pH 12-14, MANDATORY regardless of quality tier), standard 100% acrylic primer on EIFS (no alkalinity concern). Material systems: SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI (traditional) or SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ACRYLIC (EIFS). Oil-based primer is PROHIBITED on stucco. Spray on stucco = ALWAYS spray_backroll (spray-only PROHIBITED per doctrine).

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer — Spray + Back-Roll (Traditional Stucco)
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant primer by airless spray (517 tip, 60-mesh filter, 1,500-2,500 PSI) followed immediately by back-rolling with thick-nap roller (nap matched to texture profile). Back-rolling forces primer into porous stucco texture for continuous protective film. Two-person operation. Single coat. Material system: SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. No holidays or thin spots. Back-roll immediately.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. Back-roll within 30-60 seconds of spray. Inspect for complete coverage in texture valleys.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Every pore and texture valley saturated. Inspect under raking light on primary elevations.

tasks.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer — Roll Application (Traditional Stucco)
tasks.description: Apply alkali-resistant primer by heavy roller (nap matched to texture profile: 3/4-1 inch smooth, 1-1/4 inch sand/lace, 1-1/2 inch dash). Work primer into all pores and texture. Single coat. Excellent mechanical bond. Material system: SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ALKALI.

quality_notes.all: Heavy pressure to work primer into stucco pores and texture valleys. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. Roller nap must match texture profile — standard 3/8 inch nap will not penetrate stucco texture.

tasks.name: Acrylic Primer — Spray + Back-Roll (EIFS)
tasks.description: Apply 100% acrylic exterior primer by airless spray (517 tip, 60-mesh filter) followed immediately by back-rolling. EIFS is smoother than traditional stucco — standard acrylic primer is suitable (no alkalinity concern). Vapor-permeable formulation preferred. Two-person operation. Single coat. Material system: SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ACRYLIC.

quality_notes.QT3: Uniform coverage. Back-roll within 30-60 seconds. Complete coverage over EIFS texture.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Complete primer film over all EIFS texture. No holidays.

tasks.name: Acrylic Primer — Roll Application (EIFS)
tasks.description: Apply 100% acrylic exterior primer by roller on EIFS surfaces. EIFS is generally smoother than traditional stucco — roller application is effective. Single coat. Material system: SYS_EXT_STCO_PRIMER_ACRYLIC.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. Work primer into EIFS texture. Vapor-permeable primer critical for EIFS moisture management.

tasks.name: Primer — Brush Detail
tasks.description: Apply primer by brush to cut-in areas, detail work around fixtures, and areas inaccessible to roller or sprayer. Both substrate types — use matching primer system (alkali-resistant for traditional, acrylic for EIFS). Not a primary field application method.

quality_notes.all: Work primer into stucco texture at detail areas. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge where meeting roller/spray areas.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Single prime coat. Applied after all prep is complete and stucco is clean and dry. Primer selection driven by substrate_type: alkali-resistant for traditional stucco, acrylic for EIFS. Allow primer to cure per product TDS before finish coat application.

sop_modules.name: Stucco Finish Coat 1
sop_modules.description: First finish coat on primed stucco. Product determined by coating_system dimension: acrylic (SYS_EXT_STCO_FINISH_ACRYLIC_STD at QT2/QT3, SYS_EXT_STCO_FINISH_ACRYLIC_PREM at QT4) or elastomeric (SYS_EXT_STCO_FINISH_ELASTOMERIC, traditional stucco only, QT3/QT4). HARD CONSTRAINT: EIFS = acrylic ONLY — elastomeric PROHIBITED on EIFS (catastrophic moisture entrapment). Spray on stucco = ALWAYS spray_backroll (spray-only PROHIBITED).

tasks.name: Acrylic Finish Coat 1 — Spray + Back-Roll
tasks.description: Apply first acrylic finish coat by airless spray (517 tip, 60-mesh filter) followed immediately by back-rolling. Spray_backroll is gold standard for stucco — forces finish into texture for proper DFT and uniform appearance. Two-person operation.

quality_notes.QT2: Even coverage. Back-roll within 30-60 seconds. No holidays.
quality_notes.QT3: Uniform mil build. Consistent roller texture. No dry spots in texture valleys.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Every texture feature fully coated. Raking light check on visible elevations.

tasks.name: Acrylic Finish Coat 1 — Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply first acrylic finish coat by heavy roller (nap matched to texture profile). Fallback for smaller areas, occupied-adjacent, or when spray is not practical. Extension poles for elevated work.

quality_notes.all: Heavy pressure to work finish into stucco texture. Even coverage. Maintain wet edge. Roller nap must match texture profile.

tasks.name: Elastomeric Finish Coat 1 — Spray + Back-Roll
tasks.description: Apply first elastomeric finish coat by airless spray (521-525 tip, 30-mesh filter, 2,300-3,000 PSI) followed immediately by back-rolling. Elastomeric is heavy-body material requiring larger tip orifice, coarser filter, and higher PSI. Target 6-10 mil DFT per coat (12-20 mil total over 2 coats). Traditional stucco ONLY — elastomeric is PROHIBITED on EIFS. Two-person operation.

quality_notes.QT3: Even heavy coverage. Back-roll immediately. Verify 6-10 mil DFT. No holidays.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect uniformity. Full DFT across entire surface including texture valleys. WFT gauge check on representative area.

tasks.name: Elastomeric Finish Coat 1 — Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply first elastomeric finish coat by heavy roller (1-1/4 to 1-1/2 inch nap). Heavy-body material requires heavy nap and heavy pressure. Multiple passes may be needed for DFT. Traditional stucco ONLY. Extension poles for elevated work.

quality_notes.all: Heavy pressure to work elastomeric into stucco texture. Multiple heavy passes may be needed to achieve 6-10 mil DFT per coat. Maintain wet edge — elastomeric is unforgiving of lap marks.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 1 — Brush Detail
tasks.description: Brush detail first coat for cut-in areas, detail work around fixtures, and areas inaccessible to roller or sprayer. Use matching finish material (acrylic or elastomeric per coating_system). Not a primary field application method.

quality_notes.all: Work finish into stucco texture at detail areas. Even coverage. Blend seamlessly into roller/spray areas.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: First finish coat. Applied after primer has cured. Spray_backroll is primary method — spray-only is PROHIBITED on stucco. Allow recoat time per product TDS before interstage/coat 2. QT2 acrylic may stop here (single finish coat on properly primed surface).

sop_modules.name: Stucco Interstage Inspection
sop_modules.description: Inspect first finish coat. Touch up defects. QT4 only: light sand if surface anomalies detected (sanding is unusual on textured stucco — inspect/touch-up is the primary interstage activity). Module skipped for QT2 single-coat acrylic systems.

tasks.name: Intercoat Inspection
tasks.description: Inspect first finish coat for holidays, runs, sags, coverage defects, and missed texture valleys. For spray_backroll: verify uniform backroll texture and complete coverage. Check for pinholes indicating incomplete backroll. For elastomeric: verify DFT target 6-10 mil per coat.

quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough. Check all elevations for obvious defects — holidays, runs, missed texture valleys.
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic inspection at 6 ft viewing distance. Raking light inspection on visible elevations. Mark all defects. WFT gauge check for elastomeric DFT verification.

tasks.name: Interstage Light Sand (QT4 Only)
tasks.description: Light sand between finish coats with 220 grit. QT4 only — rarely needed on textured stucco but required if surface anomalies detected during raking light inspection (runs, sags, nibs). Sand only on anomalies — do not attempt to sand entire textured stucco surface.

quality_notes.QT4: Light scuff sand on anomalies only. Do not attempt to sand entire textured stucco surface. Remove nibs, runs, and defects. Sand only where anomalies are marked during inspection.

tasks.name: Interstage Dust Removal (QT4 Only)
tasks.description: Dust removal after interstage sanding. Tack cloth or compressed air to remove sanding dust from stucco texture before second coat application. Paired with TSK_STCO_SAND_INTERCOAT — only runs when sanding is performed.

quality_notes.QT4: Remove all sanding dust from stucco texture. Tack cloth or compressed air. Verify no dust remains in texture valleys before coat 2.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect -> Sand (QT4 only, if anomalies detected) -> Dust removal (paired with sand) -> Allow cure -> Coat 2. Module skipped for QT2 single-coat acrylic.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs after finish coat 1, before finish coat 2. Skipped for QT2 single-coat systems.

sop_modules.name: Stucco Finish Coat 2
sop_modules.description: Second (final) finish coat. Required at QT3 and QT4 for acrylic, and mandatory for all elastomeric (2 coats required for 12-20 mil DFT). Skipped at QT2 acrylic (single coat acceptable on properly primed surface). Same application method as coat 1. HARD CONSTRAINT: EIFS = acrylic ONLY — elastomeric tasks have substrate_type guard.

tasks.name: Acrylic Finish Coat 2 — Spray + Back-Roll
tasks.description: Apply second (final) acrylic finish coat by airless spray + back-roll. Same method and configuration as coat 1. Critical for final appearance and total film build. Two-person operation.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. Consistent appearance. No visible pattern at 6 ft.
quality_notes.QT4: Uniform mil build. No visible pattern at 3 ft. Final appearance coat.

tasks.name: Acrylic Finish Coat 2 — Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) acrylic finish coat by heavy roller. Same method as coat 1. Final coat.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. Consistent roller texture. Maintain wet edge. Final coat — critical for appearance.

tasks.name: Elastomeric Finish Coat 2 — Spray + Back-Roll
tasks.description: Apply second (final) elastomeric finish coat by airless spray (521-525 tip, 30-mesh filter, 2,300-3,000 PSI) + back-roll. Target cumulative DFT 12-20 mils over 2 coats. Traditional stucco ONLY — elastomeric PROHIBITED on EIFS. Two-person operation.

quality_notes.QT3: Even coverage. Verify cumulative DFT 12-20 mils.
quality_notes.QT4: Perfect uniformity. WFT gauge verification. Cumulative DFT 12-20 mils. Final appearance coat.

tasks.name: Elastomeric Finish Coat 2 — Roll Application
tasks.description: Apply second (final) elastomeric finish coat by heavy roller. Same method as coat 1. Target cumulative DFT 12-20 mils. Traditional stucco ONLY. Final coat.

quality_notes.all: Heavy pressure. Multiple passes if needed for DFT. Maintain wet edge. Cumulative DFT target 12-20 mils. Final coat.

tasks.name: Finish Coat 2 — Brush Detail
tasks.description: Brush detail second coat for cut-in areas and detail work. Use matching finish material. Final coat for detail areas.

quality_notes.all: Final detail coat. Blend seamlessly into roller/spray areas. Even coverage.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Second and final finish coat. Same application method as coat 1. Skipped at QT2 acrylic. Elastomeric ALWAYS requires 2 coats (DFT target 12-20 mils cumulative).

sop_modules.name: Stucco Final Inspection
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough of completed stucco coating. Inspect all elevations. Holiday check with backlighting where possible. Touch up defects found.

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all elevations and inspect finished stucco for coverage consistency, holidays, and defects. Holiday check: use backlighting (late afternoon sun angle) on visible elevations to reveal thin spots and missed areas. Check texture valleys for complete coverage.

quality_notes.QT2: Ground-level walkthrough. Quick scan for obvious misses.
quality_notes.QT3: Ground-level walkthrough at 6-10 ft viewing distance. Check all elevations. Backlight check on primary elevation.
quality_notes.QT4: Ground-level with binoculars for upper elevations. 6 ft viewing standard. Raking light and backlight check on all visible elevations. Document any defects for touch-up.

tasks.name: Final Touch-Up
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during final inspection. Focus on holidays, thin spots, and texture valley coverage.

quality_notes.QT4: Fix every defect. Blend seamlessly. Final sign-off.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect all elevations -> Touch up -> Sign off.

sop_modules.name: Stucco Cleanup & Protection Teardown
sop_modules.description: Remove all protection materials, clean equipment, dispose of waste, restore site.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all stucco tape, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags, HVAC covers, and plastic sheeting. Check for tape residue on stucco (red stucco tape can leave adhesive if overexposed to UV).

quality_notes.all: Check for tape residue. Remove all protection materials completely. Inspect landscape for overspray. Clean any overspray from hardscape immediately (easier when fresh).

tasks.name: Tool and Equipment Cleaning
tasks.description: Flush airless sprayer (full flush cycle). Clean tips and filters. Inspect tips for wear (textured stucco causes accelerated tip wear). Clean roller frames, dispose of saturated thick-nap covers. Clean brushes.

quality_notes.all: Full flush cycle for sprayer — elastomeric materials are especially important to flush completely (heavy-body material clogs equipment). Tips and filters cleaned and stored. Roller covers disposed of properly.

tasks.name: Waste Disposal and Site Cleanup
tasks.description: Collect all debris — caulk tubes, tape, plastic sheeting, paint cans, used roller covers, brush containers, sandpaper. Leave site clean and restored to pre-work condition.

quality_notes.all: Site restored to pre-work condition. All materials and debris removed. Check for staining on walkways/patios.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Protection teardown -> Tool cleaning -> Waste disposal and site cleanup.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Finish Coats (QT3/QT4, Both Substrate Types)
round_configurations.description: Standard stucco sequence: 1 primer (alkali-resistant for traditional, acrylic for EIFS) + 2 acrylic finish coats.
round_configurations.notes: Standard for QT3/QT4 acrylic on both substrate types. Primer + 2 finish coats.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 1 Finish Coat (QT2, Both Substrate Types)
round_configurations.description: Economy stucco sequence: 1 primer + 1 acrylic finish coat. Single finish coat acceptable on properly primed surface.
round_configurations.notes: QT2 economy. Single acrylic finish coat on primed stucco. Elastomeric not available at QT2.

round_configurations.name: Prime + 2 Elastomeric Finish Coats (Traditional Stucco QT3/QT4)
round_configurations.description: Elastomeric sequence: 1 alkali-resistant primer + 2 elastomeric finish coats. Target cumulative DFT 12-20 mils. Traditional stucco ONLY — elastomeric PROHIBITED on EIFS.
round_configurations.notes: Elastomeric 2-coat system. Higher DFT per coat. Traditional stucco only. Elastomeric not available at QT2.

key_stucco_rules_enforced: Crack assessment = FIRST task in prep (>1/8 inch = HARD STOP).
EIFS knock test mandatory for EIFS substrate (delamination = HARD STOP).
Spray on stucco = ALWAYS spray_backroll (spray-only PROHIBITED per Exterior Application Methods Doctrine Part A §6).
Crew size 2 for spray_backroll (one sprays, one follows with roller).
Alkali-resistant primer MANDATORY on ALL new traditional stucco (pH 12-14).
Standard acrylic primer for EIFS (no alkalinity concern).
HARD CONSTRAINT: EIFS = acrylic coating ONLY — elastomeric PROHIBITED (catastrophic moisture entrapment).
Elastomeric not available at QT2 (application complexity exceeds economy scope).
Oil-based products PROHIBITED on stucco (both traditional and EIFS).
Moisture test is a hard stop (MC >12% = do not coat) — traditional stucco only.
EIFS insurance verification required before starting EIFS work.
Texture profile drives DUAL multiplier on labor AND material — handled by FAC_STCO_TEXTURE_PROFILE modifier at production/estimation level.
Pressure wash branched by substrate_type: 1,500-3,000 PSI traditional vs <500 PSI EIFS.

assumptions.value: Traditional stucco: 1,500-3,000 PSI power wash. EIFS: <500 PSI gentle wash with wide fan tip.
assumptions.note: EIFS is vulnerable to impact damage from high-pressure water. Separate wash tasks with different PSI limits.

assumptions.value: Spray on stucco = auto-add backroll. Spray-only is PROHIBITED on porous/textured stucco.
assumptions.source: Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine.md Part A §6: 'Stucco and porous masonry: Spray bridges over pinholes/voids; back-rolling forces coating into pores'
assumptions.note: Explicit doctrine. Applies to ALL coatings on stucco: primer and finish.

assumptions.value: Elastomeric coatings are STRICTLY PROHIBITED on EIFS — causes catastrophic moisture entrapment
assumptions.note: EIFS relies on vapor permeability for moisture management. Elastomeric (5-15 perms, 12-20 mil DFT) creates a vapor barrier that traps moisture behind the system, causing EPS degradation and structural damage.

assumptions.value: Crack assessment is ALWAYS the first prep task — before any other work begins
assumptions.note: Cracks >1/8 inch indicate structural movement requiring engineering evaluation. No point in doing any other prep if the substrate has structural issues.

assumptions.value: Red stucco poly tape required instead of standard blue tape for masking ON textured stucco surfaces
assumptions.note: Exterior_Protection_Doctrine does not specifically address tape selection for rough stucco surfaces. Standard blue tape does not adhere to textured stucco. Red stucco poly tape is the field-standard solution.

assumptions.value: Light sanding between coats is unusual on textured stucco — QT4 only, and only if anomalies detected
assumptions.source: Research and field practice; confirmed by resolution.json interstage module notes
assumptions.note: Doctrine is silent on whether interstage sanding applies to textured stucco. Stucco texture makes full-surface sanding impractical. Sand only on anomalies (runs, sags, nibs).

assumptions.value: EIFS insurance verification is an administrative gate task, not a physical prep task
assumptions.note: CGL policies commonly exclude EIFS work. Verification is a project management task but included in prep module to ensure it is not skipped.
